issues.description: The getter for the boolean attribute 'excellentEnough' is implemented with an unexpected parameter in the solution: isExcellentEnough(boolean strictCheck). The problem statement requires public getters for all attributes (implying a no-argument boolean getter, typically isExcellentEnough()). This parameter mismatch will prevent student implementations from matching the expected getter signature and will likely fail automated tests that check the constructor and getters.
issues.suggestedFix: Remove the parameter from the boolean getter and provide a standard no-argument getter: public boolean isExcellentEnough() { return excellentEnough; }. Ensure the constructor and other getters remain as specified (double excellencyLevel, boolean excellentEnough, List<Ride> rides).

issues.description: The problem statement (UML and requirements) defines an attribute 'excellentEnough' in ExcellenceLand and requires public getters for all attributes (no parameters). In the solution, the corresponding accessor is implemented as isExcellentEnough(boolean strictCheck) — a method with a boolean parameter — instead of a parameterless getter. This diverges from the expected getter signature and may confuse students about the required accessor for the 'excellentEnough' attribute.
issues.suggestedFix: Provide a parameterless public getter for the 'excellentEnough' attribute to match the UML and requirements. For example: public boolean isExcellentEnough() { return excellentEnough; } (or public boolean getExcellentEnough()), and remove or rename the existing isExcellentEnough(boolean) method if any distinct behavior is needed.
